name: Aplos
summary: Fund accounting built for nonprofits and faith-based organisations, tracking restricted and unrestricted money separately. A 50%-off-for-three-months promotion was running again in September 2026, under a new code and to a new date, so check what month four costs.
best_for: small nonprofits and faith-based organisations that need true fund accounting rather than general small-business bookkeeping — tracking restricted and unrestricted funds separately is the thing generic tools genuinely cannot do
skip_if: you are a normal for-profit business, because you are paying for fund accounting you will never use; also skip it if two users on the entry tier does not cover your team and the next tier up is out of budget
honest_knock: The headline you will see first is not the price you will pay. The 50%-off banner sits at the top of the page and rewrites every figure on it. So the $39.50 that catches your eye is a three-month rate against a $79 list price. That is a 100% increase waiting in month four, on software that holds your books and is therefore painful to leave. The second thing to pin down is users: Lite includes two, and for a nonprofit with a bookkeeper, a treasurer and a director that is already tight, so establish the per-user cost before you commit.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Lite · billed monthly, as published for all three tiers
pricing.notes: (2026-09-10, read on their own pricing page) Three published tiers, billed monthly: Lite at $79/month, Core at $129 and Advanced at $229, plus a fourth Custom tier with tailored pricing aimed at organisations above $1 million in annual revenue. Advanced is framed as a quote rather than a checkout: the card reads "Customized solutions start at $229/month" and the button asks for a demo. A promotion was running when we re-read the page on 10 September 2026 — 50% off for three months with code FALL26, showing Lite at $39.50 and Core at $64.50 — and the footnote dates it: new customers only, ending 30 September. The earlier SUMMER26 promotion that ran to 31 August has been replaced on the same terms. What matters is still what you pay in month four. The trial is 15 days and takes no credit card. Lite and Core each include 2 users; Advanced includes 3.

cost_traps.label: Per-seat pricing
cost_traps.evidence: The second thing to pin down is users: Lite includes two, and for a nonprofit with a bookkeeper, a treasurer and a director that is already tight, so establish the per-user cost before you commit.

compare_with.name: QuickBooks
compare_with.why: the comparison every nonprofit treasurer ends up making, and it turns on one question rather than price. QuickBooks is cheaper and more widely known, but it tracks classes, not funds — so restricted and unrestricted money live in the same pot with a label on top. If your auditor or your grant terms require true fund separation, that difference is the whole decision and the price gap is secondary
